title: runtime: tighten KV cache compaction thresholds to prevent memory pressure spikes in cost-efficient tier
author: Omar El-Sayed
release_notes: Fixes an OOM / elevated timeout edge-case in cost-efficient batching tier under high-concurrency + long-context mixes by making KV cache compaction engage earlier and adding a hard safety cap on compaction debt.
body:
Context
During tiered batching benchmark sweeps (benchmark-lab concurrency x prompt-length buckets), we hit an edge-case where the cost-efficient tier could enter sustained KV cache memory pressure without tripping OOM guardrails soon enough. This manifested as:
- GPU memory climbing over ~60–120s and then sudden OOM on a subset of SKUs
- increased tail latency (p99) prior to the OOM due to allocator churn + late compaction
- follow-on timeouts/cancellations from overload protection (load-shed), creating noisy signals in canary

Root cause
Cost-efficient tier increases batching aggressiveness and allows higher KV cache occupancy. Our existing KV cache compaction policy was tuned for standard tier and relied on:
- a relatively high compaction trigger watermark (KV bytes as % of device)
- a compaction step size that was too small under sustained decode-heavy load
- a "compaction debt" accumulator that could grow when request mix oscillated (long-context prefill spikes + high decode concurrency)

In benchmark runs with mixed long-context prompts and high concurrency, the compaction debt could lag behind allocations, causing a delayed response: memory would continue to climb until allocator failed, rather than stabilizing.

What changed
1) Earlier compaction engagement for cost-efficient tier
- Lowered the compaction_trigger_watermark for cost-efficient (tier default) while keeping existing values for fast/standard.
- Added a second trigger based on rate-of-change (slope) of KV bytes over a short window to catch rapid growth even before hitting the absolute watermark.

2) Hard cap on compaction debt
- Introduced max_compaction_debt_bytes (per device) to prevent the scheduler from carrying excessive deferred compaction work.
- When the cap is hit, we apply an immediate compaction step sized to restore headroom, and we annotate the reason code for observability.

3) Safer behavior under fragmentation
- If compaction is engaged but allocator reports fragmentation pressure (high allocation retries), we bias toward larger compaction steps (bounded) to converge faster.

4) Observability
- Added counters + histograms to see this in prod/canary:
  - runtime_kv_compaction_trigger_total{reason=tier_watermark|slope|debt_cap|fragmentation}
  - runtime_kv_compaction_debt_bytes (gauge)
  - runtime_kv_bytes (gauge) and runtime_kv_headroom_bytes (derived)
- Added trace span annotations for compaction reason and before/after KV bytes (helps correlate with latency spikes).

Files / areas touched (high level)
- runtime/scheduler/kv_cache_compaction.{cc,h}
- runtime/scheduler/tier_defaults.yaml
- runtime/metrics/kv_cache_metrics.{cc,h}
- runtime/config/schema/runtime_config.schema.json
- runtime/tests/kv_cache_compaction_test.cc
- perf/perf_canary/scenarios/tiered_profiles.yaml

Illustrative snippet (policy)
- cost-efficient: compaction_trigger_watermark: 0.86 -> 0.81
- new: compaction_slope_trigger_bytes_per_s: 1.2GiB/s (tier-gated)
- new: max_compaction_debt_bytes: 2.0GiB (tier-gated)

Testing
- Unit: new kv_cache_compaction tests covering slope trigger + debt cap behavior (synthetic allocation patterns)
- Integration: ran tiered profile E2E on staging for chat/completions with long-context mix (128 -> 8k tokens), concurrency 16/32/64
- Bench: reran benchmark-lab corpus subset that previously OOMed (A100-80G + L40S); memory now stabilizes with <2% throughput hit vs prior cost-efficient baseline

Results (representative)
- Previously failing scenario: cost-efficient, concurrency=64, long-context bucket (6k–10k prompt)
  - before: OOM within 2–4 min; p99 latency degraded ~25–40% before failure
  - after: no OOM in 30 min run; p99 within +4% of pre-OOM window; timeouts reduced to baseline

Rollout / risk
- Change is tier-gated; default behavior for fast/standard is unchanged.
- Safe to enable behind existing tiered batching feature flag.
- Proposed canary signal for auto-rollback: any sustained increase in runtime_kv_compaction_trigger_total{reason=debt_cap} + elevated timeout rate (route-level) for >10 min.

Follow-ups
- Consider persisting these thresholds in model registry per GPU SKU for cost-efficient tier (currently tier default + SKU override table in runtime).
- Add dashboard panel to tiered batching view: KV headroom + compaction triggers by reason.

Checklist
- [x] Added/updated config docs in schema comments
- [x] Added tests (unit + staging run notes)
- [x] Added metrics with labels aligned to observability standards
- [x] No API breaking changes

Review conversation (highlights)
- Sofia Ivanova: "Can we ensure slope trigger doesn’t flap on bursty prefill?" -> Added 5s EMA smoothing and minimum window count.
- Lena Fischer: "Why cap at 2GiB?" -> Derived from worst-case debt observed in sweep; prevents runaway while keeping compaction amortized.
- Rafael Mendes: "Need a clear rollback signal." -> Added explicit debt_cap trigger counter + updated canary checklist link in description.

CI
- build-and-unit-tests: PASS
- runtime-sanitizers: PASS
- perf-smoke (tiered profiles subset): PASS
- lint/config-schema-validation: PASS

Merge
Squash merged to main; will ship with runtime-1.21 flag ramp (cost-efficient tier) once canary is green for 24h.
